title: Choose the cw-code working state
question: Same product structure in all three: projects and sessions on the left, conversation in the center, contextual tools on the right. Choose the default emphasis, or steer what should be combined.

options.label: Balanced T3
options.lineage: T3 Code structure, Rider surfaces, VS Code tooling density
options.thesis: The current three-region shell, cleaned up and scaled properly, with Diff open beside the active conversation.
options.viewport: A 296px grouped-session sidebar, fluid conversation, and roughly 500px contextual Diff pane. The center stays dominant and the right pane remains collapsible and resizable.
options.risk: Keeping the right pane open reduces the conversation width on smaller screens.

options.label: T3 Focus
options.lineage: T3 Code’s open conversation field with cw-code’s existing panel toggle
options.thesis: The same shell with the right workspace collapsed, letting the active thread and composer use the full remaining width.
options.viewport: The project/session sidebar remains fixed; the thread expands and a tiny far-right control restores Files, Diff, Agents, or Terminal.
options.risk: Tool state is less visible until the developer restores the contextual workspace.

options.label: T3 Workbench
options.lineage: T3 Code shell with a VS Code-style split inside the existing right workspace
options.thesis: The same shell while reviewing changes: Diff and Terminal share a wider contextual workspace without taking over the conversation.
options.viewport: The left session structure is unchanged; the center remains a readable thread; the right workspace expands and splits internally between Diff and Terminal.
options.risk: This state is intentionally dense and should be entered by the user rather than forced as the default.
